{{Use list-defined references|date=February 2024}}
'''Sarah''' ('''Sally''') '''Newcomb Whitney Thurston''' (born 1956)<ref name=apf>{{cite book |title=American presidential families |date=1993 |publisher=Macmillan Publ. Co. [u.a.] |location=New York |isbn=9780028973050 |page=492}}</ref> is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]] and [[environmental statistics|environmental statistician]] whose research involves the application of [[Bayesian hierarchical modeling]] to problems in [[environmental health]], including work on [[endocrine disruptors]], the effects of [[mercury in fish]] on [[prenatal development]], and the health effects of [[air pollution]]. She is a professor of biostatistics and a professor of environmental science in the Department of 
Biostatistics and Computational Biology at the [[University of Rochester Medical Center]].{{r|urmc}}

==Education and career==
Thurston majored in biology at [[Oberlin College]], graduating in 1978. After earning a master's degree in natural resources from [[Cornell University]] in 1991, she went to [[Harvard University]] for doctoral study in statistics. She earned a second master's degree in 1992 before completing her Ph.D. in 1997.{{r|cv}} Her doctoral dissertation, '' Error Analysis of Food Stamp Microsimulation Models'', was jointly advised by Alan M. Zaslavsky and [[Donald Rubin]].{{r|mg}}

She stayed at Harvard as a postdoctoral research fellow (1997–2000) and research associate (2000–2002) before moving to her present position at the [[University of Rochester]] in 2002. She added a second affiliation in oncology in 2005, and was tenured in 2008.{{r|cv}}

==Personal life==
Thurston is the daughter of mathematician [[Hassler Whitney]].{{r|hassler|dull}} Her mother Mary Barnett Garfield was a granddaughter of [[Harry Augustus Garfield]] and great-granddaughter of [[James A. Garfield]].<ref name=apf/>

==Recognition==
Thurston became an Elected Member of the [[International Statistical Institute]] in 2006.{{r|cv}} She is a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]], elected in 2019.{{r|asaf}}
